三站都在：① 三只烧杯与石墨电极、② 干电池组与双量程电流表、③ Ba(OH)₂: All three stations are here: ① three beakers with graphite electrodes, ② dry cell pack and dual-range ammeter, ③ Ba(OH)₂ titration beaker and burette. The ammeter now reads 15 mA (sample = 0.10 mol/L NaCl solution, power on), conductivity 12.6 mS/cm
三只杯子里有两只是对照：蒸馏水与 0.10 mol/L NaCl 溶液，中间那只: Two of the three beakers are controls, distilled water and 0.10 mol/L NaCl solution; the middle one is the "test sample".
电流表是唯一能把「有没有导电」变成数的仪器（分度 1 mA）。: The ammeter is the only instrument that turns "does it conduct" into a number (1 mA divisions).
湿手的危险不在水，在水把汗里的盐变成了能自由移动的离子。: The danger of wet hands isn't the water itself; water turns the salt in sweat into freely moving ions.
去掉这一步：学生只记住「湿手触电」，说不出跟电解质有什么关系。: Skip this step and students only remember "wet hands get shocks" without seeing the link to electrolytes.
常考：电解质的定义与「湿手触电」的解释——人的手上常沾有 NaCl，遇水形成电解: Commonly tested: the definition of an electrolyte and the explanation of "shocks from wet hands": hands often carry NaCl, which forms an electrolyte solution with water (Required Book 1, p.15).
人的手上常会沾有 NaCl（汗液的成分之一），当遇到水时形成电解质溶液；电解质溶: Hands often carry NaCl (one component of sweat), which forms an electrolyte solution with water; electrolyte solutions conduct, so touching a power source with wet hands easily causes a shock (textbook wording).
一勺干燥的 NaCl 固体，为什么接上电源电流表一动不动？: Why doesn't the ammeter move at all with a spoonful of dry NaCl solid connected?
把形态从「干燥固体」拖到「加热熔融」，盯住电流表: Drag the state from "Dry solid" to "Molten", watching the ammeter
干燥 NaCl 固体 0 mA、电导率 0.00 mS/cm（离子被束缚在晶体里: Dry NaCl solid 0 mA, conductivity 0.00 mS/cm (ions are locked in the crystal and can't move freely); melted, 25 mA, 3600 mS/cm (ions move faster and overcome their attractions); power off returns to 0 mA
「干燥固体不导电」不等于「NaCl 不是电解质」——电解质看的是水溶液里或熔融状: "The dry solid doesn't conduct" doesn't mean "NaCl isn't an electrolyte": electrolytes are judged by conducting in aqueous solution or when molten.
熔融也导电，说明离子本来就在晶体里，只是被束缚住了。: The melt conducts too, showing the ions were in the crystal all along, just held in place.
熔融读 25 mA 是被 60 Ω 限流电阻压进量程的，熔体本身导电能力比溶液强: The molten reading of 25 mA is held within range by the 60 Ω limiting resistor; the melt itself conducts far better than the solution.
去掉这一步：学生把「不导电」直接读成「非电解质」（教材练习 2 的 A 项就是这: Skip this step and students read "doesn't conduct" as "non-electrolyte" (exactly the mistake in option A of textbook exercise 2).
高频：电解质定义的完整表述（水溶液里或熔融状态下能导电的化合物）；「KNO₃ 固: Frequently tested: the full definition of an electrolyte (a compound that conducts in aqueous solution or when molten); what's wrong with "solid KNO₃ doesn't conduct, so it isn't an electrolyte".
能导电的物质必须具有能自由移动的、带电荷的粒子；干燥的 NaCl 固体里 Na⁺: A conducting substance must have freely moving charged particles; in dry NaCl solid, Na⁺ and Cl⁻ are tightly packed and can't move freely, and melting produces freely moving ions (textbook wording).
A4.1、A4.2、A4.4、A4.7、A4.3、标准值表 4/5、D1、D2: A4.1, A4.2, A4.4, A4.7, A4.3, standard values tables 4/5, D1, D2
同一勺 NaCl，加水搅一搅就导电了，水做了什么？: Add water to the same spoonful of NaCl and stir, and it conducts. What did the water do?
把形态拖到「水溶液」，看电流表和溶液里的离子: Drag the state to "Aqueous solution" and look at the ammeter and the ions in the solution
溶液 15 mA、12.6 mS/cm，小读数「离子能不能自由移动」变成「有（N: Solution 15 mA, 12.6 mS/cm; the small reading "can the ions move freely" changes to "Yes (Na⁺, Cl⁻ move freely)"; compare with 25 mA for the melt. Ionization equation NaCl = Na⁺ + Cl⁻
电离是溶解（或熔化）时自动发生的，不需要通电（教材练习 2 的 D 项就错在这里: Ionization happens on its own when dissolving (or melting); it doesn't need current (option D of textbook exercise 2 gets this wrong).
溶液与熔体都导电，但离子的来源不同：一个靠水分子拉开，一个靠加热克服作用力。: Both the solution and the melt conduct, but the ions come about differently: water molecules pull them apart in one, heat overcomes the attractions in the other.
电离方程式用等号（强电解质），离子符号就是溶液里实际存在的粒子。: Ionization equations use an equals sign (strong electrolytes), and the ion symbols are the particles actually present in solution.
去掉这一步：学生以为「通电才电离」，后面的离子方程式就全写反。: Skip this step and students think "current causes ionization", and every later ionic equation comes out backwards.
高频：写电离方程式（NaCl、KNO₃、HCl、H₂SO₄）；「电离需要通电吗」: Frequently tested: writing ionization equations (NaCl, KNO₃, HCl, H₂SO₄); "does ionization need current?".
电解质溶于水或受热熔化时，形成自由移动的离子的过程叫做电离；水分子把 Na⁺、C: When an electrolyte dissolves in water or melts, the process of forming freely moving ions is called ionization; water molecules pull Na⁺ and Cl⁻ off the crystal surface as freely moving hydrated ions (textbook wording).
A4.5、A4.8、A2.1、A5.2、标准值表 1、D3: A4.5, A4.8, A2.1, A5.2, standard values table 1, D3
蒸馏水是水，蔗糖溶液也是液体，为什么都测不出电流？: Distilled water is water, and sucrose solution is a liquid too. Why does neither give a current?
把物质从「蒸馏水」拖到「蔗糖」，再拖回「NaCl」对照: Drag the substance from "Distilled water" to "Sucrose", then back to "NaCl" for comparison
蒸馏水 0 mA（电导率 0.00 mS/cm——严格说纯水也导电，只是极弱，这: Distilled water 0 mA (conductivity 0.00 mS/cm; strictly, pure water conducts too, just too weakly for this setup to detect); sucrose solution 0 mA, small reading "No (sucrose doesn't ionize)"; the 0.10 mol/L NaCl control stays at 15 mA
「能导电」不是电解质的判据——铜丝、石墨都导电，但它们是单质。: "Conducts" isn't the test for an electrolyte: copper wire and graphite conduct, but they're elements.
「溶于水」也不够——蔗糖溶得很好，一点电流也没有。: "Dissolves in water" isn't enough either: sucrose dissolves well and gives no current at all.
蒸馏水那一格的 0 是「这套装置测不出」，不是「绝对不导电」（教材脚注专门交代）: The 0 for distilled water means "this setup can't detect it", not "it doesn't conduct at all" (the textbook footnote points this out).
去掉这一步：学生把「有液体、有电流」混为一谈，遇到非电解质就答不出原因。: Skip this step and students lump "there's a liquid" with "there's a current" and can't explain non-electrolytes.
高频：电解质 / 非电解质 / 单质的区分（教材练习 2 的 B 项、练习 4: Frequently tested: telling electrolytes / non-electrolytes / elements apart (option B of textbook exercise 2, ion coexistence in exercise 4).
电解质必须是化合物，且在水溶液里或熔融状态下能导电；蔗糖溶于水不电离，溶液里没有: An electrolyte must be a compound that conducts in aqueous solution or when molten; sucrose doesn't ionize in water, so its solution has no freely moving ions and doesn't conduct.
A4.1（含脚注）、A4.3、A4.4、标准值表 7/8、D1: A4.1 (with footnote), A4.3, A4.4, standard values tables 7/8, D1
都是 0.10 mol/L 的一元酸，盐酸 21 mA、醋酸只有 1 mA，差在: Both are 0.10 mol/L monoprotic acids, yet hydrochloric acid gives 21 mA and acetic acid only 1 mA. What's the difference?
把物质从「盐酸」拖到「醋酸」，看电流、电导率与电离度: Drag the substance from "Hydrochloric acid" to "Acetic acid" and look at the current, conductivity and degree of ionization
盐酸 21 mA、42.6 mS/cm（全部电离，H⁺ 与 Cl⁻ 各 0.10: Hydrochloric acid 21 mA, 42.6 mS/cm (fully ionized, 0.10 mol/L each of H⁺ and Cl⁻); acetic acid 1 mA, 0.52 mS/cm (only 1.32 % ionized, c(H⁺) about 1.3×10⁻³ mol/L, 1/76 of hydrochloric acid at the same concentration); one ionization equation uses an equals sign, the other a reversible arrow
（选必1 内容）比较两种电解质「谁导电强」必须同浓度、同温度——否则比的是浓度不: (Selective Book 1 content) Comparing "which electrolyte conducts better" requires the same concentration and temperature; otherwise you're comparing concentrations, not strength.
（选必1 内容）弱电解质的电离是可逆的，写可逆号；它的溶液里分子与离子同时存在。: (Selective Book 1 content) Weak electrolyte ionization is reversible and written with a reversible arrow; its solution contains both molecules and ions.
（选必1 内容）「强电解质的导电能力一定更强」是错的：极稀的盐酸可以比很浓的醋酸: (Selective Book 1 content) "A strong electrolyte always conducts better" is wrong: very dilute hydrochloric acid can conduct worse than very concentrated acetic acid (textbook exercise 5(1)).
去掉这一步：学生把「强弱电解质」当成「导电能力的排名」，遇到浓度差就判反。: Skip this step and students treat "strong vs weak electrolyte" as "a conductivity ranking" and get it backwards when concentrations differ.
高频：强 / 弱电解质的判断与电离方程式写法；导电能力比较的前提（同浓度、同温度: Frequently tested: identifying strong / weak electrolytes and writing their ionization equations; the precondition for comparing conductivity (same concentration, same temperature), Selective Book 1, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.
相同物质的量浓度的盐酸和醋酸的 pH、导电能力都有差别，说明两种酸中 H⁺ 浓度: Hydrochloric acid and acetic acid at the same molar concentration differ in pH and conductivity, showing their H⁺ concentrations, and so their degrees of ionization, differ: HCl ionizes completely, CH₃COOH only partly (textbook wording).
A1.6、A4.13、A2.7、A7.9、A7.10、标准值表 9/10、D4: A1.6, A4.13, A2.7, A7.9, A7.10, standard values tables 9/10, D4
往 Ba(OH)₂ 溶液里一滴滴加稀硫酸，电流为什么会先降到 0 再回升？: Adding dilute sulfuric acid drop by drop to Ba(OH)₂ solution, why does the current fall to 0 and then rise again?
把滴入体积从 0 拖到 20.0 mL，注意 10.0 mL 那一刻: Drag the added volume from 0 to 20.0 mL, paying attention to the moment at 10.0 mL
V = 0 → 19 mA（26.1 mS/cm）；5.0 mL → 14 mA: V = 0 → 19 mA (26.1 mS/cm); 5.0 mL → 14 mA; 10.0 mL → 0 mA (lowest conductivity, most white precipitate at the bottom); 15.0 mL → 15 mA; 20.0 mL → 18 mA (slightly below the start, since the system is diluted)
20.0 mL 0.05 mol/L Ba(OH)₂ + 0.10 mol/L: 20.0 mL 0.05 mol/L Ba(OH)₂ + 0.10 mol/L dilute sulfuric acid
电流下降不是「电池没电了」，是能自由移动的离子被沉淀带走。: The falling current isn't "the battery running down"; freely moving ions are being carried off by the precipitate.
最低点在 10.0 mL：Ba²⁺ 与 OH⁻ 刚好够和滴进来的 H⁺、SO₄²: The minimum is at 10.0 mL: Ba²⁺ and OH⁻ are just enough to react completely with the H⁺ and SO₄²⁻ added.
最低点不是「没有反应」，恰恰是「反应刚好做完了」——导电能力约为 0 说明溶液里: The minimum isn't "no reaction"; it's precisely "the reaction has just finished". Conductivity near 0 means there are almost no freely moving ions left (textbook question 9 ②).
去掉这一步：学生只会背「生成沉淀」，看不出导电能力曲线和离子数量是同一件事。: Skip this step and students only memorize "a precipitate forms", not seeing that the conductivity curve and the number of ions are the same thing.
高频：导电能力曲线的最低点、恰好完全反应的判断、离子方程式的书写（必修1 p.2: Frequently tested: the minimum of the conductivity curve, identifying exact complete reaction, writing the ionic equation (Required Book 1, p.21, exercise 9).
SO₄²⁻ 与 Ba²⁺ 发生反应，生成难溶的 BaSO₄ 白色沉淀；电解质在溶: SO₄²⁻ reacts with Ba²⁺ to form a sparingly soluble white BaSO₄ precipitate; reactions of electrolytes in solution are essentially reactions between ions (textbook wording).
A1.5、A5.5、A2.3、A2.6、标准值表 12–15、D6、D7、D12: A1.5, A5.5, A2.3, A2.6, standard values tables 12–15, D6, D7, D12
电流归零的那一刻，杯子里到底还剩什么？: At the moment the current hits zero, what's actually left in the beaker?
点一下台面后排的放大视窗，看离子往哪边走、沉淀怎么长出来: Tap the magnified window at the back of the bench to see which way the ions go and how the precipitate grows
视窗里阳离子向负极侧聚、阴离子向正极侧聚（各 8 个，示意放大）；滴定段 Ba²: In the window, cations gather toward the negative side and anions toward the positive side (8 of each, schematic close-up); during titration Ba²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ approach each other and combine into white BaSO₄ grains that settle to the bottom (up to 10), with fewer and fewer ions in solution; at 10.0 mL there's almost nothing but water
Na⁺ → 负极侧 · Cl⁻ → 正极侧: Na⁺ → negative side · Cl⁻ → positive side
离子只在溶液里移动，电子只在导线里移动，两条路不串。: Ions move only in the solution and electrons only in the wire; the two paths never cross.
阳离子去负极侧、阴离子去正极侧——两个方向相反，别看反。: Cations go to the negative side, anions to the positive side, in opposite directions; don't swap them.
沉淀不是「消失了」，是以白色固体沉在杯底；溶液里能动的离子少了，电流就小了。: The precipitate hasn't "disappeared"; it settles as a white solid at the bottom. With fewer mobile ions in solution, the current drops.
去掉这一步：学生能背曲线形状，但说不出「离子去哪儿了」。: Skip this step and students can recite the curve's shape but can't say "where the ions went".
高频：离子迁移方向；沉淀型离子反应的微观解释。: Frequently tested: the direction of ion migration; the microscopic explanation of precipitation reactions.
带正电荷的水合钠离子向与电源负极相连的电极移动，带负电荷的水合氯离子向与电源正极: Positively charged hydrated sodium ions move toward the electrode connected to the negative terminal, and negatively charged hydrated chloride ions toward the electrode connected to the positive terminal; SO₄²⁻ and Ba²⁺ combine into a sparingly soluble white BaSO₄ precipitate (textbook wording).
如果把稀硫酸换成稀盐酸，那条「先降后升」的曲线还会有吗？: If dilute sulfuric acid is replaced with dilute hydrochloric acid, is there still a "fall then rise" curve?

换成稀盐酸后：0 → 19 mA、10.0 mL → 15 mA、20.0 mL: With dilute hydrochloric acid: 0 → 19 mA, 10.0 mL → 15 mA, 20.0 mL → 11 mA, falling steadily with no minimum; no white precipitate (Ba²⁺ stays in solution because BaCl₂ is soluble); the current never drops to 0. （课件加的对照，教材未做）「先降后升」的形状来自 BaSO₄ 沉淀带走离子，不是: (A control added by this lesson, not in the textbook) The "fall then rise" shape comes from BaSO₄ precipitation removing ions, not from "neutralization" itself.
中和只把 H⁺ 与 OH⁻ 变成水；换成盐酸时 Ba²⁺、Cl⁻ 还在，导电能力: Neutralization only turns H⁺ and OH⁻ into water; with hydrochloric acid, Ba²⁺ and Cl⁻ remain, so conductivity drops only a little.
教材题 9 的 ③ 项说 BC 段靠过量 Ba(OH)₂ 导电，是错的——恰好反: Item ③ of textbook question 9, saying segment BC conducts because of excess Ba(OH)₂, is wrong: after exact reaction, it's the acid that's in excess.
去掉这一步：学生把「最低点」归因于「中和完成」，换个滴定剂就解释不了。: Skip this step and students attribute the "minimum" to "neutralization being complete" and can't explain it when the titrant changes.
高频：题 9 四个判断项；离子反应发生的条件（生成沉淀 / 气体 / 水）。: Frequently tested: the four statements in question 9; conditions for ionic reactions (forming a precipitate / gas / water).
复分解反应发生的条件之一是生成沉淀：Ba²⁺ 与 SO₄²⁻ 生成难溶的 BaS: One condition for a double displacement reaction is forming a precipitate: Ba²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ form sparingly soluble BaSO₄; with hydrochloric acid only neutralization occurs, the number of ions doesn't fall, and the volume just increases and dilutes it.

滴定剂保持稀硫酸，把滴入体积调到 10.0 mL（±0.5 mL），让电流 ≤: Keep dilute sulfuric acid as the titrant, set the added volume to 10.0 mL (±0.5 mL) so the current is ≤ 2 mA, and hold for 15 seconds; partway through it will be pushed to 20.0 mL
达标横幅「导电能力 · 找到终点」；进入 5 s 后滴定剂被推到 20.0 mL: Pass banner "Conductivity · endpoint found"; at 5 s the titrant is pushed to 20.0 mL (current 0 → 18 mA), and you must drag it back to 10.0 mL. Reference: 0 mA at 10.0 mL, 2 mA at 9.5 mL, 4 mA at 10.5 mL

找最低点就是找「离子最少」的那一点，电流表比看沉淀更灵敏。: Finding the minimum means finding the point with "fewest ions"; the ammeter is more sensitive than watching the precipitate.
滴定剂必须是稀硫酸——换成盐酸不会有最低点，钩子在这里。: The titrant must be dilute sulfuric acid; hydrochloric acid has no minimum. That's the catch here.
体积只差 0.5 mL，电流就差好几 mA，所以滑块步长是 0.5 mL，达标窗: Just 0.5 mL off changes the current by several mA, so the slider step is 0.5 mL and the pass window is ±0.5 mL (two steps).
没有新内容：第 6、8 步都做对，这里就是把它们同时照顾好。: Nothing new: get steps 6 and 8 right, and here you just handle both at once.
满分结构：稀硫酸 + 10.0 mL + 电流 ≤ 2 mA 保持 15 s。: Full-marks structure: dilute sulfuric acid + 10.0 mL + current ≤ 2 mA held for 15 s.
考核没有新结论：恰好完全反应时，溶液里的 Ba²⁺ 与 OH⁻ 刚好被滴进来的: The assessment has no new conclusion: at exact complete reaction, the Ba²⁺ and OH⁻ in solution are just used up by the added SO₄²⁻ and H⁺, freely moving ions are fewest, and conductivity is lowest.

本班目标：在 Ba(OH)₂ 溶液中滴入稀硫酸，找到电流最低的那一点——滴定剂选: Class goal: add dilute sulfuric acid to Ba(OH)₂ solution and find the point of lowest current: titrant dilute sulfuric acid, volume 10.0 mL (±0.5 mL), current ≤ 2 mA held for 15 seconds
KNO₃ 固体不导电，所以 KNO₃ 不是电解质: Solid KNO₃ doesn't conduct, so KNO₃ isn't an electrolyte
铜丝、石墨都能导电，所以它们都是电解质: Copper wire and graphite conduct, so they're both electrolytes
熔融的 MgCl₂ 能导电，所以 MgCl₂ 是电解质: Molten MgCl₂ conducts, so MgCl₂ is an electrolyte
NaCl 溶于水，在通电条件下才能发生电离: NaCl only ionizes in water when current is passed
电解质是「在水溶液里或熔融状态下能够导电的化合物」；KNO₃ 固体不导电是因为离: An electrolyte is "a compound that conducts in aqueous solution or when molten"; solid KNO₃ doesn't conduct because its ions can't move freely, and conducting when molten proves it's an electrolyte. Copper wire and graphite are elements; ionization doesn't need current (Required Book 1, p.20, exercise 2).
H₂SO₄ 要写 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻；弱电解质 CH₃COOH 用可逆号；K: H₂SO₄ must be written 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻; the weak electrolyte CH₃COOH uses a reversible arrow; the nitrate ion in KNO₃ is NO₃⁻. Strong electrolytes ionize completely and use an equals sign (Required Book 1, p.16).
同体积、同浓度的盐酸与醋酸，导电能力差别明显，主要原因是: Hydrochloric acid and acetic acid of the same volume and concentration differ clearly in conductivity, mainly because
醋酸不与水混合: Acetic acid doesn't mix with water
醋酸只有部分电离，溶液中离子浓度小: Acetic acid only partly ionizes, so its ion concentration is low
醋酸分子比盐酸分子大: Acetic acid molecules are bigger than hydrochloric acid molecules
盐酸是酸，醋酸不是酸: Hydrochloric acid is an acid and acetic acid isn't
导电能力取决于自由移动离子的浓度与电荷。HCl 全部电离，CH₃COOH 只有约: Conductivity depends on the concentration and charge of freely moving ions. HCl ionizes completely, while CH₃COOH only ionizes about 1.32 % (α = √(Ka/c)), so its ion concentration is far lower (Selective Book 1, Exp. 3-1).
向 Ba(OH)₂ 溶液中逐滴加入稀硫酸，导电能力先减小后增大的原因是: When dilute sulfuric acid is added dropwise to Ba(OH)₂ solution, conductivity first falls and then rises because
BaSO₄ 不是电解质，生成的沉淀不导电: BaSO₄ isn't an electrolyte, and the precipitate doesn't conduct
Ba²⁺ 与 OH⁻ 被沉淀和中和带走，恰好完全反应时离子最少，之后过量的稀硫酸: Ba²⁺ and OH⁻ are removed by precipitation and neutralization, ions are fewest at exact complete reaction, and then excess dilute sulfuric acid ionizes to give ions
水的量增加了，所以导电能力变大: There's more water, so conductivity rises
温度升高使离子运动加快: The temperature rises and ions move faster
BaSO₄ 难溶但溶解的部分完全电离，它仍是强电解质；导电能力下降是因为溶液中自: BaSO₄ is sparingly soluble but the dissolved part ionizes completely, so it's still a strong electrolyte; conductivity falls because freely moving ions are removed by precipitation and neutralization. After exact complete reaction, excess dilute sulfuric acid ionizes to H⁺ and SO₄²⁻ and conductivity recovers (Required Book 1, p.21, exercise 9 ②④).
Ba(OH)₂ 溶液与稀硫酸反应的离子方程式是: The ionic equation for the reaction of Ba(OH)₂ solution with dilute sulfuric acid is
易溶且易电离的物质写成离子形式：Ba(OH)₂ 拆成 Ba²⁺ + 2OH⁻，H: Soluble, readily ionized substances are written as ions: Ba(OH)₂ as Ba²⁺ + 2OH⁻, H₂SO₄ as 2H⁺ + SO₄²⁻; BaSO₄ is sparingly soluble and H₂O keeps its formula. Answering "Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ = BaSO₄↓" leaves out the neutralization (Required Book 1, p.18, three-step method).
接通电源后，NaCl 溶液中离子的运动方向是: With the power on, ions in NaCl solution move as follows
Na⁺ 与 Cl⁻ 都向负极侧移动: Both Na⁺ and Cl⁻ move to the negative side
Na⁺ 向正极侧、Cl⁻ 向负极侧移动: Na⁺ moves to the positive side, Cl⁻ to the negative side
Na⁺ 向负极侧、Cl⁻ 向正极侧移动: Na⁺ moves to the negative side, Cl⁻ to the positive side
离子在溶液中不动，只有电子在动: Ions don't move in the solution; only electrons move
带正电荷的水合钠离子向与电源负极相连的电极移动，带负电荷的水合氯离子向与电源正极: Positively charged hydrated sodium ions move toward the electrode connected to the negative terminal, and negatively charged hydrated chloride ions toward the electrode connected to the positive terminal (Required Book 1, p.16, Fig. 1-12).
滴定剂换成稀硫酸：生成 BaSO₄ 沉淀，电流会先降后升: Titrant switched to dilute sulfuric acid: BaSO₄ precipitates and the current falls, then rises
滴定剂换成稀盐酸：只中和不沉淀（课件加的对照，教材未做），电流只随稀释略降、没有: Titrant switched to dilute hydrochloric acid: neutralization only, no precipitate (a control added by this lesson, not in the textbook); the current only drops slightly from dilution, with no minimum
电源断开：电流为 0，但溶液的电导率没有变——断的是回路，不是电离: Power off: the current is 0, but the solution's conductivity hasn't changed. What's broken is the circuit, not the ionization
异常：滴定剂被推到 20.0 mL——电流回到 18 mA，把它拖回 10.0: Fault: the titrant was pushed to 20.0 mL. The current is back to 18 mA, so drag it back to 10.0 mL

本课目标：先看干燥固体与熔融的区别（电解质看的是「水溶液里或熔融状态下」），再看: Lesson goal: first see the difference between a dry solid and a melt (electrolytes are judged "in aqueous solution or when molten"), then how ions are freed from the crystal; next compare strong and weak electrolytes at the same concentration; finally add dilute sulfuric acid and read "exact complete reaction" from the minimum of the conductivity curve: when ions are carried off by the precipitate, the current drops.
示意声明：电流表量程与分度（0–30 mA / 0–300 mA）、电源电压 1: Disclaimer: the ammeter ranges and divisions (0–30 mA / 0–300 mA), 1.5 V supply, 60 Ω limiting resistor, 50 m⁻¹ cell constant, electrolyte concentrations (the textbook only says "dilute solution"; 0.10 mol/L is from Selective Book 1, Exp. 3-1), Ba(OH)₂ and dilute sulfuric acid concentrations and volumes, and conductivity values are teaching illustrations (lesson settings).
